title: Battle of Plassey
description: The East India Company defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah at Plassey, establishing British dominance in Bengal.

title: Battle of Buxar
description: Company victory over Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Shah Alam II consolidated British political power in eastern India.

title: Grant of Diwani Rights
description: Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company revenue collection rights over Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

title: Great Bengal Famine of 1770
description: A catastrophic famine wiped out approximately one-third of Bengal's population due to drought and exploitative company revenue policies.

title: Calcutta Becomes Capital of Company Rule
description: Warren Hastings transferred administrative seats to Calcutta, making it the primary hub of British power in India.

title: Establishment of Supreme Court of Judicature
description: The Regulating Act of 1773 led to the establishment of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Calcutta.

title: Asiatic Society Founded
description: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta to promote Oriental research and studies.

title: Permanent Settlement of Bengal
description: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement, creating a new landlord (zamindari) system across Bengal.

title: Fort William College Established
description: Lord Wellesley established Fort William College in Calcutta, fostering the formalization of modern prose in Indian languages.

title: Hindu College Founded
description: Hindu College (later Presidency University) was established in Calcutta, initiating modern Western education in Bengal.

title: Birth of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
description: Birth of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, polymath, key reformer of the Bengal Renaissance, and champion of women's rights.

title: Brahmo Samaj Founded
description: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj), spearheading socio-religious reform.

title: Abolition of Sati
description: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck formally banned the practice of Sati following intense advocacy by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

title: Young Bengal Movement
description: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio's radical teachings led to the Young Bengal movement, sparking freethinking among youth.

title: Calcutta Medical College Established
description: Medical College, Bengal was established in Calcutta, making it the first medical institution in Asia teaching Western medicine.

title: Birth of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
description: Birth of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, author of 'Anandamath' and composer of India's national song 'Vande Mataram'.

title: First Passenger Train in Eastern India
description: The first passenger train service in Eastern India operated between Howrah and Hooghly.

title: Santhal Rebellion (Hool)
description: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal rebellion against British colonial authorities and the zamindari system.

title: Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act
description: Legislation legalizing the remarriage of Hindu widows was enacted following campaigns by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

title: University of Calcutta Established
description: The University of Calcutta was incorporated, becoming the first multidisciplinary modern university in South Asia.

title: Mangal Pandey Rebellious Revolt
description: Mangal Pandey revolted against British officers at Barrackpore, sparking events of the Revolt of 1857.

title: Indigo Revolt (Nil Bidroha)
description: Farmers across Bengal staged a widespread revolt against forced indigo cultivation by European planters.

title: Birth of Rabindranath Tagore
description: Birth of Rabindranath Tagore, Asia's first Nobel Laureate, poet, philosopher, and cultural icon.

title: Calcutta High Court Established
description: The High Court of Judicature at Fort William was established under the High Courts Act 1861.

title: Birth of Swami Vivekananda
description: Birth of Narendranath Datta (Swami Vivekananda), spiritual leader and founder of Ramakrishna Math and Mission.

title: Indian Association Founded
description: Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose established the Indian Association in Calcutta to advocate political rights.

title: Publication of Anandamath
description: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay published 'Anandamath', containing the poem 'Vande Mataram'.

title: Ramakrishna Mission Founded
description: Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission at Belur Math near Calcutta.

title: Birth of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
description: Birth of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, legendary Indian nationalist leader.

title: Anushilan Samiti Formed
description: Pramathanath Mitra and Satischandra Mukherjee established Anushilan Samiti, promoting revolutionary nationalist activities.

title: First Partition of Bengal
description: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal Presidency into West Bengal and East Bengal with Assam.

title: Launch of Swadeshi Movement
description: Protests against the Partition of Bengal initiated the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement in Town Hall, Calcutta.

title: Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case
description: Following the Muzaffarpur bombing, British authorities arrested Sri Aurobindo and revolutionaries of Anushilan Samiti.

title: Annulment of Partition & Capital Shift to Delhi
description: King George V announced the annulment of Bengal's partition and shifted British India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi.

title: Tagore Awarded Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Rabindranath Tagore was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for 'Gitanjali'.

title: Visva-Bharati University Inception
description: Rabindranath Tagore formally inaugurated Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan.

title: Chittagong Armoury Raid
description: Surya Sen (Masterda) led Indian revolutionaries to seize the police armoury in Chittagong.

title: Writers' Building Attack
description: Benoy Basu, Badal Gupta, and Dinesh Gupta assassinated Inspector General of Prisons N.S. Simpson inside Writers' Building.

title: Netaji's Great Escape from Calcutta
description: Subhas Chandra Bose escaped British house arrest from his Elgin Road residence in Calcutta.

title: Bengal Famine of 1943
description: A devastating war-induced famine led to millions of civilian deaths across Bengal.

title: Direct Action Day & Great Calcutta Killings
description: Widespread communal violence broke out in Calcutta following the Muslim League's call for Direct Action Day.

title: Tebhaga Movement Begins
description: Peasant uprising organized by Kisan Sabha demanding a two-thirds share of harvested crops for sharecroppers.

title: Partition of Bengal and Birth of West Bengal
description: Bengal was partitioned upon Indian independence; Hindu-majority West Bengal joined India, while East Bengal joined Pakistan.

title: Prafulla Chandra Ghosh Becomes First Chief Minister
description: Prafulla Chandra Ghosh took office as the first Chief Minister of West Bengal.

title: Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy Appointed Chief Minister
description: Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy became Chief Minister, embarking on a 14-year period that laid West Bengal's modern infrastructure.

title: Princely State of Cooch Behar Merged with West Bengal
description: Cooch Behar officially merged with the Indian Union and became a district of West Bengal.

title: Nehru-Liaquat Pact Signed
description: Bilateral treaty signed to protect minority rights and manage massive post-Partition refugee influx into West Bengal.

title: First West Bengal Legislative Assembly Election
description: Indian National Congress won the inaugural assembly elections, securing Dr. B.C. Roy's leadership.

title: Inception of Durgapur Steel Plant
description: Government initiated planning for Durgapur Steel Plant, transforming Durgapur into the industrial hub of West Bengal.

title: Integration of French Chandannagar into West Bengal
description: Former French enclave of Chandannagar formally merged into Hooghly district of West Bengal.

title: Satyajit Ray Releases Pather Panchali
description: Satyajit Ray's debut film 'Pather Panchali' premiered, placing West Bengal cinema on the global artistic map.

title: States Reorganisation Act Redraws West Bengal Borders
description: Bengali-speaking regions of Bihar (Purulia and parts of Islampur) were transferred to West Bengal.

title: 1959 Food Movement (Khaddya Andolan)
description: Massive price-rise resistance led by Left parties climaxed in severe police crackdowns in Calcutta.

title: IIM Calcutta Established
description: Indian Institute of Management Calcutta was established as the first national institute for post-graduate management.

title: Death of Dr. B.C. Roy & Prafulla Sen CM
description: Chief Minister Dr. B.C. Roy passed away; Prafulla Chandra Sen assumed office as the next Chief Minister.

title: Formation of CPI(M)
description: Communist Party of India split at the Seventh Congress, creating CPI(M), which would heavily shape West Bengal politics.

title: Naxalbari Uprising
description: Peasant uprising in Naxalbari village led by Charu Majumdar initiated the far-left Naxalite movement in India.

title: First United Front Government Formed
description: Non-Congress coalition government formed with Ajoy Mukherjee as CM and Jyoti Basu as Deputy CM.

title: Dismissal of First United Front Ministry
description: Governor dismissed the United Front government, appointing Prafulla Chandra Ghosh in a short-lived ministry.

title: First President's Rule Imposed in West Bengal
description: Central Government imposed President's Rule following political instability and cabinet collapses.

title: Second United Front Government Formed
description: United Front returned to power after mid-term elections with Ajoy Mukherjee as CM.

title: Completion of Farakka Barrage Construction
description: Farakka Barrage across the Ganges was completed to flush the Hooghly river and preserve Kolkata Port.

title: Massive Refugee Influx During Bangladesh Liberation War
description: Over 7 million refugees fled East Pakistan into West Bengal, creating critical logistical and political challenges.

title: Siddhartha Shankar Ray Becomes Chief Minister
description: Congress returned to power under Siddhartha Shankar Ray amidst allegations of rigged assembly elections.

title: 1974 Smallpox Epidemic
description: A severe smallpox epidemic broke out in West Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha, killing thousands before eradication drives succeeded.

title: State of Emergency Imposed
description: National Emergency proclaimed; political opponents and Naxalite suspects faced severe state repression in West Bengal.

title: Left Front Comes to Power (Jyoti Basu CM)
description: Left Front won a landslide assembly victory, beginning 34 years of uninterrupted rule with Jyoti Basu as CM.

title: Launch of Operation Barga
description: Left Front launched Operation Barga to record and protect sharecroppers' land rights across rural West Bengal.

title: Marichjhapi Eviction Incident
description: Forcible police eviction and blockade of East Bengali refugee settlers on Marichjhapi island in the Sundarbans.

title: India's First Underground Metro Opens in Calcutta
description: Kolkata Metro began commercial operation between Esplanade and Bhowanipore, India's first underground railway.

title: Gorkhaland Movement Escalates
description: Subhash Ghisingh led the Gorkha National Liberation Front (GNLF) demanding a separate state for Darjeeling hills.

title: Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council Formed
description: Tripartite accord created the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council, granting autonomous administrative powers.

title: Inauguration of Second Hooghly Bridge (Vidyasagar Setu)
description: Vidyasagar Setu cable-stayed bridge opened, creating a second major linkage over the Hooghly River.

title: July 21 Writers' Building March Firing
description: Police opened fire on a Youth Congress march led by Mamata Banerjee near Writers' Building, killing 13 workers.

title: Trinamool Congress Formed
description: Mamata Banerjee broke away from the Congress party to form All India Trinamool Congress (AITC).

title: Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee Sworn In as Chief Minister
description: Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee succeeded Jyoti Basu as Chief Minister, focusing on industrialization drives.

title: Calcutta Officially Renamed to Kolkata
description: The official name of West Bengal's capital city was changed from Calcutta to Kolkata.

title: Singur Anti-Land Acquisition Protests
description: Protests erupted against land acquisition for the Tata Nano car factory in Singur, sparking a major political shift.

title: Nandigram Violence & Police Firing
description: Police firing on anti-SEZ land acquisition protesters in Nandigram caused 14 deaths, sparking widespread outrage.

title: Tata Motors Relocates Nano Plant Out of West Bengal
description: Tata Motors announced the exit of its Nano project from Singur following prolonged political agitation.

title: Lalgarh Anti-Police Santras Committee Protests
description: Tribal uprising in Lalgarh against police excesses turned into a conflict involving Maoist insurgents and joint forces.

title: Historic Election Win Ends 34-Year Left Front Rule
description: Trinamool Congress-led alliance defeated the Left Front in assembly elections, ending 34 years of Communist rule.

title: Mamata Banerjee Sworn In as First Female Chief Minister
description: Mamata Banerjee took the oath of office, becoming the first female Chief Minister of West Bengal.
